    TAKE THIS WITH YOU
    The Prompt Critic's Checklist
    • Give the who, what, when and where. Copilot only knows what you tell it; which carpark, which dates, which office.
    • Keep people's personal and health details out of prompts. De-identify first; the story can be told without the name.
    • Name the audience and how they read. Plain English and short sentences are a choice you make, not a fluke.
    • Supply the facts. Copilot fills every gap with something plausible; it will not say "I don't know".
    • Never send your worst mood. Ask for the tone you want to be known for; the email carries your name, not Copilot's.
    • If it isn't public, it doesn't go in the prompt. Add links yourself, afterwards; a prompt is a disclosure.
    • Say what you want. Format, length, key points, and what the reader should do next.
    • Copilot drafts, you decide. Proofread every draft; the last check is always human.
